course: Pizza Oven Construction - Wood Fired 12 Pizza

lessons.title: Designing Chimney Height and Diameter
lessons.body: For a 12-inch pizza oven, the chimney must be sized right to pull smoke out without cooling the oven. A common rule: chimney diameter should be 1/6 to 1/8 of the oven's internal diameter. For a 12-inch oven, that means a 2-inch (50mm) to 2.5-inch (63mm) flue. If you go too wide, smoke lingers; too narrow, and you choke the fire. Use a tape measure and a steel pipe or clay flue tile that matches. Height matters more than diameter. The chimney should rise at least 3 feet (900mm) above the oven's dome, and extend at least 2 feet (600mm) above any roof ridge within 10 feet (3m). In many African settings, ovens sit under a simple tin roof or in an open-air kitchen. If the chimney exits through a roof, add 2 feet above the roofline. A taller chimney increases draft, but too tall (over 6 feet above the dome) can make the oven hard to heat because too much heat escapes. For most small bakeries, a total chimney height of 4 to 5 feet (1.2 to 1.5m) from the oven floor works well. Mark the height on a wall or stick, and cut your pipe or stack bricks to that length. Always check local wind patterns: in coastal areas, a shorter, wider chimney may handle gusts better. In still inland areas, a taller chimney helps. Use a level to keep the chimney plumb; a leaning chimney will smoke into the room. Finally, consider the materials: mild steel pipe is cheap but rusts; clay flue tiles are traditional and handle heat, but crack if heated too fast. For a 12-inch oven, a single 2.5-inch clay flue tile or a 2-inch steel pipe is sufficient. Calculate the cross-sectional area: for a 2-inch pipe, area = Ï Ã (1 inch)Â² â 3.14 square inches. This matches the small firebox. Write down your design before you build.

lessons.title: Installing a Chimney Pipe or Brick Flue
lessons.body: You have two main choices: metal pipe or brick flue. Metal pipe is faster and cheaper. Use black steel pipe (not galvanized, which releases toxic fumes when heated) of 2-inch or 2.5-inch diameter. Start at the oven's top opening. The first section should be at least 12 inches (300mm) long and sit directly over the smoke hole. Secure it with a high-temperature sealant or fire cement. If using a brick flue, you will build a square or rectangular column of firebricks from the oven dome up. The internal flue size should match the design (e.g., 2.5 inches square). Lay bricks with fire clay mortar, leaving a smooth inner surface. A rough interior creates turbulence and reduces draft. For a 12-inch oven, a brick flue of 3 inches internal diameter is common. Start by building a base collar around the oven opening: a ring of bricks or a metal plate with a hole cut for the flue. This prevents smoke from leaking at the joint. For metal pipe, use a damper or a sliding plate at the base to control airflow. Install the pipe in sections, each overlapping the lower one by 2 inches (50mm) to shed rain and prevent leaks. Use three metal screws at each joint. For brick flue, build in stages, checking plumb with a spirit level every three courses. Allow mortar to cure for 24 hours before firing. In Africa, many builders use locally made clay pipes or even old stove pipes. Ensure they are clean and free of holes. If using a 90-degree elbow to exit a wall, keep the horizontal run under 12 inches (300mm) to maintain draft. Support the pipe every 3 feet (900mm) with metal straps or brackets. Never use plastic or PVC. After installation, test for smoke leaks by burning paper at the oven opening and watching for smoke escaping at joints. Seal any leaks with fire cement. A well-installed flue lasts for years.

lessons.title: Creating a Smoke Chamber and Baffle
lessons.body: The smoke chamber is the space just above the oven dome and below the chimney. Its shape affects how well smoke exits. For a 12-inch oven, the smoke chamber should be a funnel that narrows from the full oven opening (about 12 inches wide) to the chimney diameter (2.5 inches) over a height of 6 to 8 inches (150-200mm). This funnel shape speeds up smoke and prevents backdraft. Build it with firebricks or a metal cone. If using bricks, corbel each course inward by 1 inch (25mm) until you reach the flue size. Use fire clay mortar. A baffle is a metal plate or brick shelf that sits inside the smoke chamber to deflect smoke and keep heat in the oven. Position the baffle at the top of the oven opening, angled downward toward the oven floor by about 30 degrees. It should cover about 2/3 of the opening, leaving a gap for smoke to pass. This forces smoke to travel a longer path, giving it time to cool slightly and deposit creosote, but more importantly, it reduces the chance of smoke rolling out into your face when you open the door. For a 12-inch oven, a baffle made from a 6-inch by 8-inch piece of 3mm steel plate works well. Weld or bolt it to the smoke chamber walls. Alternatively, a row of bricks set at an angle can serve as a baffle. Ensure the baffle does not block more than 70% of the opening, or you will choke the fire. Test the baffle by lighting a small fire and watching smoke: it should curl up and out, not spill into the room. Adjust the angle if needed. In many African kitchens, a simple metal hood over the oven opening can act as a smoke chamber, but a proper brick funnel is more durable. Keep the smoke chamber clean of soot; a buildup can restrict flow. Brush it monthly.

lessons.title: Sealing Chimney Joints to Prevent Leaks
lessons.body: Smoke leaks at chimney joints waste heat, stain walls, and can be dangerous. Every joint between pipe sections, or between the flue and the oven, must be sealed. For metal pipe, use a high-temperature silicone sealant rated to 600Â°F (315Â°C) or fire cement. Apply a bead around the male end of the pipe before inserting it into the female end. Then secure with three sheet metal screws. For brick flues, seal the mortar joints with fire clay mortar, and after curing, paint the exterior with a refractory coating or a thin slurry of fire clay and water. At the base, where the flue meets the oven dome, use a collar of fire cement or a metal flange bolted to the oven top. This is the most common leak point. Pack the gap with ceramic fiber rope or fire cement. For a 12-inch oven, a 2-inch wide strip of ceramic fiber rope around the flue base works well. If you have a damper, seal its frame to the flue with fire cement. In Africa, many builders use a mixture of clay, sand, and cow dung as a sealant. While traditional, it cracks over time. Better to use commercial fire cement if available. Test for leaks by burning a smoky fire (green leaves or wet wood) and watching for smoke escaping at joints. You can also hold a lit candle near joints; if the flame flickers inward, there is a leak. Seal any leak immediately. For metal pipes, check for rust holes; replace rusted sections. For brick flues, repoint any cracked mortar. Remember, a sealed chimney draws better and keeps your kitchen free of smoke. Do this job carefully, and you will avoid headaches later.

lessons.title: Testing Draft and Smoke Draw
lessons.body: Before you fire your oven for baking, test the draft. Draft is the upward pull of air through the chimney. A good draft carries smoke away quickly. To test, light a small fire of dry paper and kindling in the oven. Hold a lit match or incense stick near the oven opening. The smoke should be drawn into the oven and up the chimney, not blown back into the room. If smoke spills out, you have a draft problem. Common causes: chimney too short, flue too narrow, or a cold chimney. On a cold start, preheat the flue by burning a rolled-up newspaper held near the chimney opening for 30 seconds. This warms the air and starts the draft. For a 12-inch oven, a chimney height of 4 feet above the dome usually gives good draft. If draft is weak, increase height by adding a section, or reduce restrictions. Check for blockages: birds nests, soot, or a closed damper. Use a mirror and flashlight to inspect the flue. Another test: light a candle and place it in the oven opening. The flame should lean toward the chimney. If it stands straight or blows out, draft is poor. You can also use a smoke pencil (a stick of incense) and watch the smoke trail. In African conditions, wind can cause downdraft. If your chimney is on the windward side, a chimney cap or a rotating cowl can help. Test on a still day first. If draft is good, you will see smoke rise steadily and no smoke in the room. If not, adjust: open a window or door slightly to provide makeup air. A sealed kitchen with no air inlet will starve the fire and cause smoke. After testing, note the best damper position for your oven. Mark it. Always test before each baking session, especially if the weather changed.

lessons.title: Adding a Chimney Cap and Spark Arrestor
lessons.body: A chimney cap keeps rain, birds, and debris out of your flue. A spark arrestor is a mesh screen that stops hot sparks from flying out and starting fires on your roof or nearby. For a 12-inch oven, a simple cap can be made from a metal bucket or a piece of sheet metal bent into a cone. It should sit at least 2 inches (50mm) above the flue opening and be 4 inches (100mm) wider than the flue diameter. This allows smoke to escape but blocks rain. For a 2.5-inch flue, a cap of 6 inches diameter works. Attach it with three metal legs or a strap. Do not block the opening completely; smoke must exit. A spark arrestor is a metal mesh (1/4-inch or 6mm openings) wrapped around the top of the chimney or fitted inside the cap. Use galvanized or stainless steel mesh, not plastic. In Africa, many hardware stores sell mosquito netting, but that is too fine and clogs quickly. Use coarse mesh. To install, cut a piece of mesh 12 inches by 6 inches, roll it into a cylinder, and secure it with wire inside the cap. Or buy a ready-made spark arrestor. Check it monthly; clean with a wire brush. A clogged arrestor reduces draft. In areas with strong winds, add a wind vane or a rotating cowl to the cap. This turns with the wind and always faces downwind, improving draft. For brick flues, a simple concrete cap with a mesh screen works. Make sure the cap is heavy enough not to blow off. In bushfire-prone areas, spark arrestors are mandatory. Even in towns, they prevent roof fires. After installing, test the draft again. The cap should not reduce draw. If smoke backs up, remove the cap and check for blockage. A well-fitted cap and arrestor make your oven safer and more reliable.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Chimney and Venting Systems for Wood-Fired Pizza Ovens

In a commercial wood-fired pizza operation â whether you are baking 12-inch pizzas in Nairobi's Kilimani, Lagos's Lekki, or Accra's Osu â the chimney is not a decorative afterthought. It is the engine that drives combustion, controls smoke, protects your staff, and determines whether you can legally operate near neighbours. A poorly designed flue will cost you fuel, slow your bake, blacken your pizzas, and invite a visit from environmental health officers. This Practical Reference lesson gives you the numbers, materials, and field-tested methods to build a chimney that works the first time.

Why Draft Matters More Than You Think

Draft is the pressure difference that pulls combustion gases up and out of your oven. It is created by the temperature difference between hot flue gases and cooler outside air, and by chimney height. In hot African climates, this temperature differential is smaller than in Europe, so you need a taller and better-insulated chimney to achieve the same draw. A wood-fired oven running at 400â450Â°C in the dome produces flue gas temperatures of 200â350Â°C at the chimney base. If your flue cools too quickly â common with single-skin mild steel in cold morning air â draft collapses and smoke rolls out the oven mouth into your dining area.

For a 12-pizza (approx. 1.2 m internal diameter) oven, the standard rule is a flue diameter of 150â200 mm and a total effective height of 3â4.5 m above the oven floor, with at least 1.5 m extending above the roof line. Every elbow, mesh cap, or horizontal run reduces effective draft by 10â20%, so keep the run as straight and vertical as possible.

Designing Chimney Height and Diameter

Use the table below as your field sizing guide. It assumes a 12-pizza oven with a 150â200 mm flue and a total run with no more than two 45Â° bends. If you operate in a low-wind coastal site (Mombasa, Dar es Salaam), add 0.5 m to the height. If you are in a high-altitude city (Addis Ababa, Nairobi at 1,600â2,300 m), add 0.5â1 m because lower air density weakens draft.

Table 1: Recommended chimney sizing for 12-pizza wood-fired ovens (Africa conditions)
Oven size / use Flue internal diameter Min. height above oven floor Height above roof ridge Notes
12-pizza, low output (â¤40 pizzas/hr) 150 mm 3.0 m 1.0 m Single-skin insulated flue acceptable
12-pizza, standard commercial 180 mm 3.5 m 1.5 m Preferred for most African cities
12-pizza, high output (â¥80 pizzas/hr) 200 mm 4.0 m 1.5â2.0 m Insulated double-wall or brick flue
Coastal / low-wind site 180â200 mm +0.5 m 1.5 m Corrosion-resistant cap required
High altitude (>1,500 m) 200 mm +0.5â1.0 m 1.5â2.0 m Compensate for thin air

Sources: Adapted from Brick Industry Association Technical Note 19 (Residential Chimneys) and FAO âWood-Fired Ovensâ technical briefs; altitude adjustment from standard HVAC draft formulas.

Installing a Chimney Pipe or Brick Flue

You have two realistic options in Africa: mild steel or stainless steel pipe, or fired clay brick flue. Steel is faster and cheaper to install but corrodes within 2â4 years in coastal humidity unless you use 304 or 316 stainless. Brick is more expensive up front but lasts 20+ years and gives better thermal mass â which means better draft in the morning when your oven is cold.

Steel installation: Use 2 mm minimum wall thickness for the first 1 m (the hottest section), then 1.5 mm above. Seal every joint with high-temperature silicone (rated 300Â°C+) and secure with stainless self-tapping screws. Never use galvanised pipe â zinc fumes are toxic.

Brick installation: Use firebricks or well-fired clay bricks laid with refractory mortar for the first 1 m, then ordinary mortar above. Keep the internal flue smooth â rough mortar squeeze-out creates turbulence and kills draft. A 200 mm flue should be built with a 200 mm internal former, not approximated by brick coursing.

Table 2: Material comparison for African pizza oven chimneys
Material Typical cost (USD/m) Lifespan Draft quality Best for
Mild steel pipe 8â15 2â4 yrs Moderate Low-budget startups, inland dry areas
304 stainless pipe 25â45 8â12 yrs Good Coastal cities, high-output kitchens
316 stainless pipe 40â70 15+ yrs Excellent Salt-air coastal, premium restaurants
Fired clay brick flue 30â60 20+ yrs Excellent (with mass) Permanent installations, hotels, lodges

Cost ranges from 2024 supplier quotes in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa; lifespan from Brick Industry Association TN19 and manufacturer data.

Creating a Smoke Chamber and Baffle

The smoke chamber is the transition zone between the oven dome opening and the flue. It should be funnel-shaped, narrowing from the oven mouth width to the flue diameter over a vertical rise of 300â500 mm. A flat ceiling here causes smoke to swirl and spill into the kitchen.

The baffle is a horizontal plate or angled lip inside the smoke chamber that slows the escape of hot gases, keeping heat in the dome longer and improving draft stability. Fit it 100â150 mm above the oven opening, projecting 30â50% across the chamber. In brick ovens, a simple firebrick ledge works well. In steel ovens, weld a 3 mm plate at a 30Â° downward angle toward the flue.

Sealing Chimney Joints to Prevent Leaks

Every joint is a potential leak. Leaks dilute draft, cool flue gases, and stain your walls with creosote. Use:

  • Refractory mortar for brick-to-brick joints in the hot zone.
  • High-temperature silicone (300Â°C+) for steel pipe joints.
  • Fibreglass rope gasket for expansion joints where steel meets brick.
  • Fire cement for sealing the flue collar to the oven dome.

Test each joint with a smoke pencil or incense stick while the oven is warm. Any smoke that moves sideways, not upward, is a leak.

â  SAFETY WARNING â CARBON MONOXIDE AND FIRE RISK

Wood-fired ovens produce carbon monoxide (CO), an odourless, invisible gas that kills. Never install a pizza oven chimney that terminates indoors, under a closed roof, or below an openable window. The flue must always discharge above the roof line and away from air intakes. Install a CO alarm in any indoor or semi-enclosed kitchen. In shared compounds (common in Nairobi, Kampala, and Lagos), a chimney that is too short will push smoke into neighbours' windows â this is both a health hazard and a legal liability. Check local municipal by-laws before installation; many African cities now require a minimum 1.5 m clearance above the roof and a spark arrestor.

Testing Draft and Smoke Draw

Before you fire the oven for the first time, do a cold smoke test: light a small fire or smoke source at the oven mouth and watch the smoke. It should travel straight up the flue with no hesitation. Then do a hot test: bring the oven to 300Â°C and observe. If smoke rolls out the front, your flue is too short, too narrow, or leaking. Add height first â it is the cheapest fix.

A simple draft gauge (or a piece of tissue held near the oven mouth) confirms airflow direction. If the tissue is pulled inward, draft is working. If it flutters outward, you have a problem.

Adding a Chimney Cap and Spark Arrestor

The cap keeps rain, birds, and leaves out. The spark arrestor â a metal mesh with 10â12 mm openings â prevents hot embers from landing on your roof or a neighbour's. In dry-season Africa, this is not optional. Choose a stainless cap with a removable top for cleaning. Never use a cap with mesh smaller than 10 mm; it clogs with creosote within weeks and kills draft.

Quick Reference Checklist

  1. Flue diameter 150â200 mm for a 12-pizza oven; 200 mm for high output or high altitude.
  2. Total height 3â4.5 m above oven floor; at least 1.5 m above roof ridge.
  3. Keep the run vertical; maximum two 45Â° bends, no 90Â° elbows.
  4. Smoke chamber funnel-shaped, 300â500 mm rise, with baffle 100â150 mm above opening.
  5. Seal all joints with refractory mortar or 300Â°C+ silicone; test with smoke pencil.
  6. Fit a stainless cap with a 10â12 mm spark arrestor mesh.
  7. Install a CO alarm if the oven is indoors or semi-enclosed.
  8. Run a cold smoke test and a hot test before commercial service.

Further Reading

  • FAO â Wood-Fired Ovens and Stoves Technical Briefs
  • Brick Industry Association â Technical Note 19: Residential Chimneys
  • NFPA 211 â Standard for Chimneys, Fireplaces, Vents, and Solid Fuel Appliances
  • WHO â Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality: Household Fuel Combustion
  • US DOE â Wood and Pellet Heating (venting and safety guidance)

This module is part of the RISE AFRICA Skills programme. For business planning, pair this technical lesson with our costing and licensing modules before committing to a commercial installation.

quiz.q: For a 12-inch pizza oven, what is the recommended chimney diameter?
quiz.explanation: The chimney diameter should be 1/6 to 1/8 of the oven's internal diameter, so for 12 inches, 2 to 2.5 inches is correct.

quiz.q: How high should the chimney rise above the oven dome?
quiz.explanation: A minimum of 3 feet above the dome ensures proper draft for a small oven.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid galvanized pipe for a chimney?
options: B) It releases toxic fumes when heated
D) It is hard to cut
quiz.explanation: Galvanized coatings release toxic zinc fumes when heated, so black steel is safer.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a smoke chamber?
options: B) To funnel smoke from the oven to the chimney
quiz.explanation: The smoke chamber narrows from the oven opening to the flue, speeding up smoke and preventing backdraft.

quiz.q: How much should a baffle cover the oven opening?
quiz.explanation: A baffle covering about 2/3 of the opening deflects smoke without choking the fire.

quiz.q: What is the best way to seal a metal chimney joint?
options: B) High-temperature silicone or fire cement
quiz.explanation: High-temperature sealant or fire cement withstands heat and prevents leaks.

quiz.q: How can you test for a smoke leak at a joint?
quiz.explanation: A candle flame flickering inward indicates a leak; smoke will also escape visibly.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of poor draft?
quiz.explanation: A short chimney does not create enough pressure difference to pull smoke up.

quiz.q: How can you preheat a cold chimney to start draft?
options: B) Burn a rolled newspaper near the flue
quiz.explanation: Burning paper warms the air in the flue, starting the upward flow.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a chimney cap?
options: B) To keep rain and debris out
D) To hold the chimney up
quiz.explanation: A cap blocks rain, birds, and debris while allowing smoke to escape.

quiz.q: What size mesh is recommended for a spark arrestor?
quiz.explanation: 1/4-inch mesh stops sparks but does not clog easily with soot.

quiz.q: How often should you clean a spark arrestor?
quiz.explanation: Monthly cleaning prevents clogging and maintains draft.

quiz.q: What is the correct order of building a brick flue?
options: B) Start from oven and go up
quiz.explanation: You build from the oven upward, checking plumb as you go.

quiz.q: Why is a smooth inner flue surface important?
options: B) It reduces turbulence and improves draft
quiz.explanation: A rough surface creates friction and turbulence, weakening draft.

quiz.q: What is a baffle made of in a small oven?
quiz.explanation: Steel plate or angled bricks withstand heat and deflect smoke.

quiz.q: How much horizontal run is acceptable in a chimney?
quiz.explanation: Horizontal runs reduce draft, so keep them under 12 inches.

quiz.q: What is a sign of a good draft?
options: B) Smoke rises steadily up chimney
quiz.explanation: Good draft pulls smoke up and out, leaving the room clear.

quiz.q: Why should you provide makeup air?
quiz.explanation: Without air inlet, the fire starves and smoke cannot rise.

quiz.q: What is a rotating cowl used for?
options: B) To improve draft in windy conditions
quiz.explanation: A rotating cowl turns with the wind, always facing downwind to enhance draft.

quiz.q: How can you check for a blocked flue?
options: A) Look with a mirror and flashlight
quiz.explanation: Visual inspection with a mirror and light reveals nests or soot blockages.

quiz.q: What is the minimum height above a roof ridge for a chimney?
quiz.explanation: Chimneys should extend at least 2 feet above any roof ridge within 10 feet.

quiz.q: Which material is best for sealing a brick flue exterior?
options: B) Refractory coating or fire clay slurry
quiz.explanation: Refractory coating or fire clay slurry withstands heat and seals cracks.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when installing a chimney cap?
quiz.explanation: A cap must allow smoke to escape; blocking the opening causes backdraft.

quiz.q: Why should you test draft before baking?
options: B) To ensure smoke goes out and oven heats properly
quiz.explanation: Testing ensures proper smoke draw and identifies leaks before you bake.

quiz.q: What is the recommended overlap for metal pipe sections?
quiz.explanation: A 2-inch overlap sheds rain and prevents leaks at joints.

quiz.q: How many screws per metal pipe joint are recommended?
quiz.explanation: Three screws secure the joint and keep it aligned.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a damper?
options: A) To control airflow and draft
quiz.explanation: A damper regulates the amount of air going up the chimney, controlling the fire.

quiz.q: What is a sign of a chimney leak?
quiz.explanation: Smoke smell indoors indicates a leak at a joint or base.

quiz.q: How can you make a simple spark arrestor?
options: B) Wrap coarse mesh around the flue
quiz.explanation: Coarse metal mesh (1/4 inch) wrapped around the flue stops sparks.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep the smoke chamber clean?
options: A) To prevent soot buildup that restricts flow
B) To make it look nice
quiz.explanation: Soot buildup narrows the chamber and reduces draft, so clean it monthly.
